html:
The Nanti are a small people of the headwaters of the Camisea and Timpía rivers in the southeastern Amazon of Peru. About 250 to 450 people speak Nanti, a language of the Kampa branch of the Arawakan family, close to that of the Matsigenka.

They kept apart from outsiders until the 1980s and 1990s, partly because of memories of violence in the rubber era. They live in a state reserve for isolated peoples. Since the 2000s the large Camisea natural gas project has worked nearby, raising worries about disease and the forest. Neighbours: Nomatsigenka and Kakinte.
